items.q: What makes hosting Git hard if every object already has a SHA?
items.a: **Packfiles.** Clients speak packs. A file-at-commit is a **walk** (commit → tree → blob), often through **deltas** with no DAG-to-disk locality. A KV store (SHA → object) dies on those hops. Google's JGit DHT **abandoned** it because clone was too slow.

items.q: What did GitHub's Spokes keep that the KV approach threw away?
items.a: A **real Git repo on local NVMe**, replicated at the packfile layer, kept **fully consistent**. Industry default since ~2013. Reads go to any of ≥3 machines. Writes do **prepare / lock / commit**.

items.q: What is the tail-at-scale write tax?
items.a: Four waits **per replica** on 3PC. Five nodes → 20 waits → ~**18%** chance of a P99 on the path. A viral repo (~200 waits) → ~**86%**. Add replicas for CI and **pushes get slower**.

sections.title: S3 is the repo; disks are cache

items.q: What is Continuity's source of truth?
items.a: A **write-ahead log on S3**, not the NVMe copy. Ack after persist. **Rendezvous hashing** picks a preferred node; any node can rebuild in milliseconds. Idle repos can have **zero** replicas. Origin is the product.

items.q: What did Primeagen still feel after the recap?
items.a: Smarter, and still sure he could build it. **The problem of confidence.**
